terms.sub: Red Cell Indices and Automated FBC
clues: Expressed in femtolitres (fL), with a normal adult reference interval of approximately 80 to 100 fL.
Used as the primary morphological basis for classifying anaemias into microcytic, normocytic, and macrocytic.
Calculated by dividing haematocrit by the red blood cell count to determine average erythrocyte size.

terms.sub: Red Cell Indices and Automated FBC
clues: Helps differentiate iron deficiency anaemia from uncomplicated beta-thalassaemia minor.
Quantifies the degree of anisocytosis on an automated full blood count.
The coefficient of variation of red blood cell volume distribution around the mean.

terms.sub: Peripheral Blood Film: Red Cell Morphology
clues: Corresponds directly to an elevated Red Cell Distribution Width (RDW) on automated analyzers.
Often paired with poikilocytosis on peripheral blood film reports.
Abnormal variation in the size of circulating red blood cells.

terms.sub: Peripheral Blood Film: Red Cell Morphology
clues: Also referred to as helmet cells or bite-like fragmented erythrocytes.
Generated when red blood cells are mechanically sheared by intravascular fibrin strands or prosthetic heart valves.
A fragmented red blood cell serving as the morphological hallmark of microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia.

terms.sub: Peripheral Blood Film: Red Cell Morphology
clues: Normally removed ('pitted') from circulating erythrocytes by splenic macrophages.
Frequently observed on blood smears of Nigerian patients with sickle cell anaemia who have undergone autosplenectomy.
A small, round, densely basophilic nuclear DNA remnant inside a red blood cell indicating hyposplenism.

terms.sub: Peripheral Blood Film: Red Cell Morphology
clues: Cannot be seen on routine Wright or Giemsa smears and requires supravital crystal violet staining.
Classically triggered by oxidative stress in glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency.
An intra-erythrocytic inclusion composed of precipitated, denatured haemoglobin.

terms.sub: Peripheral Blood Film: Leukocytes and Platelets
clues: Stains strongly positive for myeloperoxidase and Sudan Black B.
Formed by abnormal coalescence of primary azurophilic granules.
A pink-red needle-shaped cytoplasmic crystalline inclusion pathognomonic of acute myeloid leukaemia blasts.
Obtained exclusively from the posterior or anterior iliac crest and never from the sternum.
Essential when bone marrow aspiration results in a 'dry tap'.
A cylindrical core of intact bone and marrow sampled with a Jamshidi needle to assess marrow architecture and cellularity.
